summary: Fixed the oversized marker cursor preview: the cursor now renders the exact placed-marker geometry (capsule, outline, numeral via EditorImageRenderer.drawMarker at defaultMarkerDiameter) into a Retina-resolution bitmap, context-scaled by the live scroll magnification — so preview size equals placed bounds * magnification at fit 0.25, zoom 0.5/1/2, and everything in between, with no clamp. Refresh is driven by a synchronous boundsDidChangeNotification observer on the enclosing scroll view's clip view (attached in viewDidMoveToSuperview), which fires on every magnification change including trackpad pinch, zoom buttons/keys, and auto-fit; a didChangeBackingPropertiesNotification observer re-renders on Retina transitions. Targeted run: 26/26 marker tests pass; full suite: 255/255 pass.
findings: Root cause confirmed: markerPreviewCursor used `defaultMarkerDiameter * textCreationZoomFactor` clamped to 16...64, while the canvas is actually displayed at scrollView.magnification = baseScale * userZoomFactor (EditorWindowController.applyZoom, line ~748). At typical fit scales (~0.25) the preview was 2-4x too large; the 64pt cap also capped it wrongly at high zoom.

True canvas-to-screen factor is exactly `enclosingScrollView.magnification` — verified headless: setting NSScrollView.magnification on a documentView-embedded canvas updates the property and the clip view bounds synchronously.

Magnification changes (programmatic applyZoom AND native trackpad pinch via scrollView.magnify) both change clipView.bounds → the boundsDidChangeNotification observer catches all of them. Notification delivery is synchronous (queue: nil), so tests observe it deterministically.

markerOutlineWidth has a max(2, diameter*0.06) floor and markerFont a floor — scaling the drawing CONTEXT (not shrinking the MarkerItem) keeps outline/numeral ratios identical to placed markers, as required.

Bitmap rep user space is pixels: scale = backingScaleFactor * magnification maps canvas coords to pixels; NSImage.size stays in screen points so NSCursor displays it at exactly the on-screen marker size.
Placed marker/text creation sizing untouched — defaultMarkerDiameter still equals defaultTextFontSize; only preview rendering changed.
The observer also fires on scrolling/resize (bounds.origin/size changes) — harmless extra invalidation since cursor rect recompute is lazy.
Headless NSScrollView accepts documentView and magnification without a window, enabling the regression tests.
changes: Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift — markerPreviewCursor rewritten: builds the marker at placed geometry (diameter=defaultMarkerDiameter, centered in its markerBounds), renders into an explicit NSBitmapImageRep of size screenSize*backingScale with cgContext.scaleBy(backing*magnification), wrapped in NSImage(size: screenSize); hotspot = center; no clamp; crosshair fallback only for degenerate (<1pt) sizes.

Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift — new private canvasToScreenScale (enclosingScrollView?.magnification, finite+positive-guarded, fallback 1) and internal markerPreviewScreenSize() exposing canvasBounds*magnification for tests.

Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift — viewDidMoveToSuperview attaches a synchronous NSView.boundsDidChangeNotification observer on enclosingScrollView.contentView (enables postsBoundsChangedNotifications), invalidating the preview on any magnification change; removed on detach/deinit.

Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift — existing viewDidMoveToWindow extended with an NSWindow.didChangeBackingPropertiesNotification observer so the bitmap re-renders at the new backing factor when moving between displays.

Tests/ZoomiesTests/NumberedMarkerTests.swift — 2 new tests (24→26): testCursorPreviewMatchesPlacedMarkerScreenBoundsAcrossMagnification (embeds canvas in NSScrollView, asserts markerPreviewScreenSize == placed markerBounds * magnification for 0.25/0.5/1/2, and asserts no clamp: >64pt at 2x, <16pt at 0.25x); testCursorPreviewInvalidatesWhenScrollMagnificationChanges (hook fires on each magnification change).
Tests/ZoomiesTests/NumberedMarkerTests.swift — var→let warning fix on an unmutated binding.
decisions: Source of truth = enclosingScrollView.magnification rather than recomputing baseScale*userZoomFactor in the canvas — it is the live applied value, covering fit scale, user zoom, and pinch without duplicating controller math. Rejected convert(_:to:nil) because it requires a window (headless tests and early lifecycle can't use it).
Observer on clipView boundsDidChangeNotification (documented, synchronous) rather than KVO on NSScrollView.magnification (not documented KVO-compliant).

Explicit NSBitmapImageRep at window/screen backingScaleFactor instead of lockFocus — deterministic Retina pixel count regardless of focus/context quirks; NSImage point size remains the exact screen size so NSCursor needs no further handling.
Context scaling instead of a resized MarkerItem — preserves relative stroke widths since markerOutlineWidth/markerFont have minimums that would distort a smaller-diameter render.
Removed the 16...64 clamp entirely per report; only a <1pt degenerate guard remains, falling back to .crosshair.
evidence: Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift:1728-1733 (canvasToScreenScale), :1735-1747 (markerPreviewScreenSize), :1749-1788 (markerPreviewCursor rewrite), :1795-1815 (viewDidMoveToSuperview clipView observer), :162-176 (viewDidMoveToWindow backing observer), :1817-1826 (deinit cleanup).

Sources/EditorWindowController.swift:739-749 (applyZoom sets scrollView.magnification = baseScale*userZoomFactor), :282-289 (allowsMagnification + documentView setup), :988-995 (EditorScrollView only gates scrollWheel).

checks.detail: 26 tests, 0 failures. Two compile errors en route, both fixed: (1) didChangeBackingProperties is not an NSView method — replaced with NSWindow.didChangeBackingPropertiesNotification observer; (2) editableState() returns EditorCanvasState.Marker, not MarkerItem — test now constructs MarkerItem from state fields.
EditorScrollView only overrides scrollWheel gating; CenteringClipView only constrains bounds origin — neither blocks magnification or bounds-size notifications.

open_issues: NSCursor has undocumented maximum image dimensions; at extreme zoom (~6x) the preview approaches ~270pt — not clamped per instructions; if AppKit ever rejects oversized cursor images the fallback would need re-evaluation (not observed).
Visual confirmation in the running app not performed (install/launch prohibited; parent handles install). The geometry/equality path is covered by tests.
Cursor preview still renders on mouse-entry boundary only per cursor-rect lifecycle; magnification observer covers zoom-driven staleness.
next_steps: Parent may install the built app and smoke-check the preview at fit and after pinch zoom. No further code changes anticipated.
